newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says lira should rise before ERM reentry.
newsitem.headline: France says lira should rise before ERM reentry.

text.p: France said on Wednesday the lira should appreciate against the franc before Italy re-enters the European Monetary System's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).

President Jacques Chirac's spokeswoman, Catherine Colonna, told a briefing: "We want the lira to rejoin the ERM rapidly. Some people have talked about the coming months, perhaps even before the end of the year. That seems to us a good thing. But in any case it must occur at an appropriate level...and there is undoubtedly some catching-up to do."
Colonna clarified France's position after Chirac triggered a diplomatic row with Rome on Tuesday by saying Italy might not be fit to join a single European currency from the start in 1999.

The president retreated, praising Italy's tough budget and saying he hoped it would be in the first wave of monetary union, after Rome protested and threatened to cancel a Franco-Italian summit due to start in Naples on Thursday night.
"The movement of the lira in the past year is positive but it is no secret that we think there is still room for appreciation (against the franc)," Colonna said.

She said the Italian currency had depreciated by about 40 percent against the franc after it was ejected from the ERM in 1992, harming French industry, and had since regained about 20 percent of its value.
